messages:
maria: Quick sync — after kernel-selector v2 rolled we see a tail latency bump on production chat workloads. A100 and T4 are worst. Need to pick new max-tokens-per-batch by GPU family and adjust queue policy. Profiling below + proposed numbers.

owen: Ugh, saw the alerts. Any immediate mitigations?

maria: Canary rollback would fix but want a tuned config instead. Short profile dump:

```
profile run: conv-chat-64k
device: h100-1 | peak_throughput: 94 examples/s | p95 latency: 210ms | kv_hit: 0.72 | avg_tokens_in_batch: 48_000
device: a100-2 | peak_throughput: 68 examples/s | p95 latency: 310ms | kv_hit: 0.63 | avg_tokens_in_batch: 36_000
device: a10-3  | peak_throughput: 40 examples/s | p95 latency: 480ms | kv_hit: 0.49 | avg_tokens_in_batch: 28_000
device: t4-4   | peak_throughput: 18 examples/s | p95 latency: 820ms | kv_hit: 0.34 | avg_tokens_in_batch: 18_000
device: l4-5   | peak_throughput: 22 examples/s | p95 latency: 700ms | kv_hit: 0.40 | avg_tokens_in_batch: 12_000
```

maria: Observations: kernel selector is picking heavier kernels when avg_tokens_in_batch exceeds certain thresholds -> KV fragmentation increases -> latencies climb nonlinearly. Need both per-card max_tokens and a queue softcap to smooth bursts.

liam: Thanks. I re-ran microbenchmarks with different per-card caps. Short results:
- H100: raising cap up to 96k keeps throughput but KV fragmentation is low because kernel vLLM handles >64k well.
- A100: sweet spot ~48k, beyond that kernel fallback triggers and p95 spikes.
- A10: 32k gives best cost/latency tradeoff.
- T4: 16k (lowering from 24k) reduces tail considerably.
- L4: 12k preserves throughput, higher causes kv thrash.

owen: So proposed per-family max_tokens_per_batch: H100 96_000, A100 48_000, A10 32_000, T4 16_000, L4 12_000?

maria: That's my tentative list. Also propose queue softcap: when queue depth > 2000 tokens across waiting requests, dynamically cap forming batch to 80% of family max for 30s to let KV catch up.

kate: Can you show the config snippet for the runtime? I want to run a controlled canary.

maria: Sure — config patch (yank into canary pool):

```
batching:
  family_caps:
    h100: 96000
    a100: 48000
    a10: 32000
    t4: 16000
    l4: 12000
  queue_softcap:
    enabled: true
    token_threshold: 2000
    softcap_pct: 0.8
    cooldown_s: 30
  policy: "prefer_low_latency"
```

maria: We'll also flip kernel-selector telemetry to verbose for canary so we can map kernel choices -> kv frag.

liam: I pushed a quick perf-bot run against the canary pool (small sample, dev region). perf-bot result:

perf-bot: canary run summary (1000 reqs): H100 p95 195ms (-7%), A100 p95 295ms (-5%), T4 p95 640ms (-22%), A10 p95 450ms (-6%), L4 p95 682ms (-2%). KV hit rates up ~3-6% on all families.

owen: Nice. Any regressions in throughput or error rate?

perf-bot: errors: unchanged. throughput delta: H100 +2%, A100 -1%, A10 -1%, T4 +4% (due to less queuing/backpressure).

maria: Good sign. Next steps: schedule 25% traffic canary for next deploy window (2h), collect kernel-selection traces + kv-frag metric, and gate on p95 and kv_hit. If p95 degrades >3% for any family rollback.

kate: I’ll schedule the canary and add dashboards. Which metric names?

maria: Watch metrics: runtime.batch.p95_per_family, runtime.kv.cache.hit_rate, runtime.kernel.selector.fallback_count, runtime.queue.tokens_waiting. Also track errors and cpu/gpu utilization.

liam: Small note — if H100 spike appears during long sequences, we should allow burst override: allow H100 temporary factor 1.25 of family cap for sequences with kv_hit > 0.85. Avoids throttling high-quality cacheable traffic.

owen: Agreed — add that as a conditional. Maria can you update config?

maria: Updated config draft applied to canary: added h100_burst_override_pct: 1.25 with kv_hit floor 0.85.

maria: TL;DR decisions: apply family caps H100=96k, A100=48k, A10=32k, T4=16k, L4=12k; enable queue softcap 2000 tokens at 80% of cap with 30s cooldown; allow H100 conditional burst override (1.25x if kv_hit>=0.85). Canary 25% next window, rollback rule p95 +3% tolerance.

kate: Sounds good. I'll create the rollout ticket and dashboard. @liam can you leave the verbose kernel logs on during canary?

liam: Yep, will keep verbose for 3 hours post-deploy and then move to sampled mode.

owen: Thanks team. If canary looks good we roll global. If anything odd ping #incidents. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — copying notes into the perf runbook.
